title: Hall Coefficient Sign Reversal Driven by Orbital-Selective Oxygen-Vacancy Scattering in Nickelate Films
authors: Jian-Jian Miao, Yue Liu, Yue Zhao, Yichen Hua, Changming Yue, Wei-Qiang Chen
abstract: Hall measurements in superconducting bilayer nickelate films show sign reversals that cannot be explained by rigid-band electron doping alone. We combine a DFT+CDMFT-derived correlated multi-orbital quasiparticle model with a $T$-matrix treatment of oxygen-vacancy scattering in a semiclassical Boltzmann transport framework. We find that multiband compensation is insufficient by itself: in-plane vacancies selectively suppress the transport channel dominated by the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital and drive $R_H$ through zero, whereas inner-apical vacancies make $R_H$ more negative. These results identify pocket-resolved and orbital-selective oxygen-vacancy scattering as the microscopic origin of the Hall coefficient sign reversal and provide a framework for oxygen-stoichiometry-dependent transport in nickelate films.
summary: This theoretical study explains the anomalous sign reversal of the Hall coefficient in nickelate superconductors. The authors combine sophisticated correlated electron modeling with a Boltzmann transport approach to show that this effect arises not from simple doping, but from orbital-selective scattering caused by oxygen vacancies. This work provides a crucial microscopic understanding of stoichiometry dependence in these complex materials.
main_problem: The study aims to microscopically explain the sign reversal observed in the Hall coefficient ($R_H$) measured in superconducting bilayer nickelate films.
main_result: The sign reversal is attributed to orbital-selective scattering caused by oxygen vacancies, specifically showing that in-plane vacancies selectively suppress the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital contribution, driving $R_H$ through zero.
method: A semi-classical Boltzmann transport framework is employed, incorporating a T-matrix treatment of oxygen-vacancy scattering potentials derived from DFT+CDMFT correlated multi-orbital quasiparticle models.
model_or_system: The system is superconducting bilayer nickelate films modeled using a correlated multi-orbital quasiparticle Hamiltonian. The analysis separates doping effects from impurity-scattering effects due to oxygen vacancies (inner-apical and in-plane).
key_observables: Hall coefficient ($R_H$), pocket-resolved contributions ($	ext{R}_{	ext{u}}	ext{H}$), and orbital-selective transport components.
important_parameters: Oxygen vacancy concentration ($n_{	ext{vac}}$), chemical potential ($\mu$), and the relative scattering strength of different vacancy types (in-plane vs. inner-apical).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a T-matrix approach for scattering, solves the Boltzmann equation using the scalar relaxation-time approximation, and treats vacancies as active scattering centers rather than just dopants.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Fermi surface pockets ($\alpha,  eta, \gamma$) colored by orbital weight; plots show $R_H$ vs. vacancy concentration demonstrating sign reversal driven by in-plane defects; other figures detail the dependence of $R_H$ on scattering time and doping.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem (unexplained $R_H$ sign reversal), develops a theoretical framework combining DFT+CDMFT with Boltzmann transport, calculates pocket-resolved and orbital-selective contributions, and finally attributes the sign change to specific vacancy scattering mechanisms.
why_interesting: While focused on nickelates, the methodology—combining correlated electron models (DFT+CDMFT) with detailed impurity scattering theory within a transport framework—provides advanced techniques for analyzing how disorder affects electronic transport in strongly correlated materials.
